sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: RTK is a command-line tool that shrinks the output of shell commands before an AI coding agent reads it. Test runs, diffs, logs and builds become short summaries, which cuts the tokens your agent spends.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding agents read the full output of commands like git status or npm test, which wastes context and money. RTK hooks into the agent and rewrites those commands so the agent reads a compact version instead.
whoFor: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI users
Developers who want lower AI agent bills
Teams running agents on large codebases
Anyone curious how many tokens commands waste
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a free, install-and-forget way to cut command output for 18 coding agents. Savings apply to command output only, which is one part of your total bill.
requirements: macOS, Linux, or Windows (winget, WSL or Git Bash)

overview: After installing, rtk init adds a hook to your agent. When the agent runs git status, RTK runs rtk git status and the agent reads a few lines instead of dozens. It covers 100+ commands across Git, the GitHub CLI, Rust, JavaScript, Python, Go and more, in under 25 ms per command.

RTK promises never to block (if a filter fails you get the raw output and the original exit code), never to print more than the command did, and to say where the full output is when it cuts something. rtk bypass runs a command unfiltered, and rtk gain shows the savings recorded on your machine.

Pipelines go further: one file can hand big file reads to a cheaper model, compress more than shell output or make the agent write less. An optional proxy, under a separate BUSL-1.1 license, cleans API traffic. Telemetry is off by default.

strengths: Install once, then nothing to learn

limitations: Only command output is compressed by default; built-in Read and Grep tools pass through
Another crate named rtk exists on crates.io, so check you have the right one
The proxy has a separate BUSL-1.1 license

troubleshooting.problem: rtk gain says command not found or shows no dashboard
troubleshooting.solution: You may have a different crate named rtk. Reinstall from this project.

troubleshooting.problem: The agent still reads full output
troubleshooting.solution: Restart the agent after rtk init, and check your agent uses a hook rather than a rules file.
Run the command with rtk bypass, for example rtk bypass git log --oneline -20.

troubleshooting.problem: Does it break the prompt cache?
troubleshooting.solution: No; output is filtered once, before it enters the conversation.
